# Physics and Collision

> **Draft chapter map.** Separate gameplay spatial queries from rigid-body simulation and integrate a physics provider without surrendering World ownership.

## Collision Is More Than Physics

- Distinguish overlap tests, ray queries, character movement, triggers, and full dynamics.
- Explain why many gameplay questions do not require a costly rigid-body simulation.

### Spatial Queries as a Contract

- Define query inputs, filtering, results, and coordinate-space policy.
- Connect collision data to World state and streaming residency.

#### Broad Phase and Narrow Phase

- Explain candidate generation versus precise contact testing.
- Relate the split to data-oriented structures and performance budgets.

## Provider-Based Simulation

- Explain the value of an engine-facing physics contract over direct dependency on one library.
- Compare provider abstraction with pretending all physics engines have identical behavior.

### Bodies, Constraints, and Characters

- Cover dynamic bodies, kinematic controllers, joints, and authored collision shapes.
- Establish the ownership and synchronization rules with the game-facing World.

#### Fixed-Step Integration

- Connect simulation cadence to Chapter 4’s time model.
- Explain interpolation and event delivery at the boundary.

## Physics at Scale

- Discuss streamed collision, large coordinates, and sleeping objects.
- Connect performance policy to the world-residency model.

### Debugging and Verification

- Outline visual debug drawing, reproducible scenarios, and determinism limits.
- Explain how profiling separates query cost from solver cost.

#### Smallworld Provider Design

- Use Smallworld to illustrate the selected contract and integration path.
- Keep third-party library details subordinate to the design principles.

## Navigation Is a Separate Spatial Service

- Explain why collision answers immediate geometric questions, whereas navigation answers planned movement questions over an authored and changing world.
- Lead into the next chapter's query, threading, streaming, and budget contracts for pathfinding.
